title: What's with this "Internet of Things"?
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explain the Internet of Things: a network of connected devices with sensors that communicate with servers, usually in the cloud. They trace the term to Kevin Ashton's late-1990s idea of RFID tags on lipstick at Procter and Gamble, its predecessor ubiquitous computing, and older telemetry. They cover examples (smart thermostats, auto-ordering filters, smart toothbrushes, Waze-style traffic data, smart cities), hurdles such as incompatible protocols and the IPv4 address shortage leading to IPv6 and NAT, security and privacy concerns (Target's pregnancy-prediction ads, smart TV voice recognition terms, hacking of medical devices), economic impact and job displacement (ATMs and bank tellers). The episode ends with listener mail thanks and sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and smart gadget jokes
segments.summary: Hosts joke about a Jerome/Jerry nickname and banter about connected gadgets such as an app-controlled vaporizer and an auto-feeding cat machine, plus the concern that convenience erodes privacy.

segments.title: Defining the Internet of Things
segments.summary: The hosts define the Internet of Things as interconnected devices with sensors that communicate with central servers in the cloud, and give everyday examples such as smart thermostats, smoke detectors and exercise trackers.

segments.title: Convenience versus complication and auto-ordering
segments.summary: The hosts debate whether automation makes life simpler or more fragile, and discuss automatic delivery of filters and formula and whether devices could prompt reorders, with a joke about fridges ordering milk.

segments.title: Kevin Ashton and the origin of the term
segments.summary: Kevin Ashton is credited with coining the term Internet of Things in the late 1990s while at Procter and Gamble, proposing RFID tags on lipstick to automatically signal low stock. The hosts also discuss ubiquitous computing as a predecessor.

segments.title: Smart everyday objects and smart toothpaste
segments.summary: The hosts joke about smart toothpaste tubes and toothbrushes that track brushing, and a relative's shaving log, while noting that connected products now exist.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break with banter about brushing teeth timing, and a short sponsor/break transition.

segments.title: Telemetry and the building blocks of connected devices
segments.summary: The hosts trace telemetry to remote measurement sent over telephone lines, credit the World Wide Web and WiFi for enabling the Internet of Things, and describe the cheap components needed: computing, sensors, communication hardware and power.

segments.title: Smart cities and traffic apps
segments.summary: The hosts discuss connected traffic data, including Waze relying on user phone data and reports, and smart traffic lights and sidewalks with embedded sensors.

segments.title: Hurdles: incompatible platforms and IP address shortage
segments.summary: The hosts discuss fragmented, non-integrated smart home systems and platforms such as Qualcomm's AllSeen Alliance, Apple HomeKit, Google, Samsung, and Wink. They then cover the IPv4 address shortage, NAT as a workaround, and the move to IPv6.

segments.title: Security, privacy, Target ads and smart TV eavesdropping
segments.summary: The hosts discuss privacy and security risks of connected sensors, Target's use of credit card purchase data to predict pregnancy and target ads, Samsung's smart TV voice recognition terms, and the danger of hacked medical devices and baby monitors.

segments.title: Economics, Square, and job displacement
segments.summary: The hosts cite an estimated economic value for the Internet of Things, discuss Square as an example of democratized payments, and debate whether automation like ATMs costs or creates jobs, ending with a call for government retraining.

segments.title: Listener mail thanks
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners who sent gifts including candied pecans, whiskey, cheese, cards, and a longboard, and mention social media and contact details.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing reminder of how to find more information and the show website.
